questions.scenario: Tom owns a well-kept three-family building in an older urban neighborhood. Several insurers have declined to write fire coverage, and his agent mentions the New York Property Insurance Underwriting Association (the FAIR Plan).
questions.stem: Which statement about the association is accurate?

choices.text: It may issue coverage if an inspection finds the property insurable
choices.rationale: Correct: § 5401(g) defines insurable property as property the association determines, after inspection and under plan criteria, to be insurable.

choices.text: It must insure any building regardless of its condition
choices.rationale: Incorrect: property with ownership, condition, occupancy or maintenance characteristics that violate public policy is not insurable.

choices.text: It may decline Tom because of the neighborhood's loss history
choices.rationale: Incorrect: neighborhood or area location shall not be considered in determining insurable condition.

choices.text: It is funded by state tax revenue rather than by insurers
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the plan of operation provides for assessment of member insurers to defray losses and expenses.

questions.explanation: The FAIR Plan (NYPIUA) is a joint underwriting association of all insurers writing fire and extended coverage in New York. It provides basic property coverage on 'insurable property' — property found insurable after inspection under objective plan criteria — and neighborhood or area location may not be considered (Ins. Law §§ 5401(g), 5402).
questions.memoryTip: FAIR Plan: inspect the PROPERTY, ignore the NEIGHBORHOOD.

keyPoints.label: Property must be inspected and found insurable

questions.stem: Under NY Insurance Law § 5401, the FAIR Plan may treat property as uninsurable based on each of the following EXCEPT its:

choices.text: Physical condition that violates public policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: condition is one of the listed characteristics that can make property uninsurable.

choices.text: Occupancy that violates public policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: occupancy is a listed characteristic.

choices.text: Maintenance that violates public policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: maintenance is a listed characteristic.

choices.text: Neighborhood or area location
choices.rationale: Correct: § 5401(g) states that neighborhood or area location shall not be considered in determining insurable condition.

questions.explanation: § 5401(g): property is not insurable if it has characteristics of ownership, condition, occupancy or maintenance which violate public policy, but neighborhood or area location shall not be considered. This mirrors New York's broader ban on geographic redlining.
questions.memoryTip: Judge the building, not the block.

questions.stem: Which insurers must be members of the NY Property Insurance Underwriting Association?

choices.text: Insurers writing fire and extended coverage directly in NY
choices.rationale: Correct: § 5402(a) makes membership a condition of authority to transact fire, extended coverage and homeowners insurance in NY.

choices.text: Only insurers that volunteer to join the association
choices.rationale: Incorrect: membership is mandatory for insurers engaged in writing fire and extended coverage.

choices.text: Only insurers domiciled in the state of New York
choices.rationale: Incorrect: membership is based on writing the business in NY, not on domicile.

choices.text: Only insurers that write private passenger auto insurance
choices.rationale: Incorrect: auto insurers are associated with the auto insurance plan, not Article 54.

questions.explanation: § 5402(a): the association consists of all insurers authorized to write and engaged in writing fire and extended coverage insurance on a direct basis in New York (including in homeowners and commercial package policies), excluding assessment cooperative fire insurers. Remaining a member is a condition of continuing to write that business.
questions.memoryTip: Write fire in NY? You're in the FAIR Plan.

questions.stem: Under Article 54, 'extended coverage' written by the FAIR Plan includes direct loss caused by:

choices.text: Flood and surface water
choices.rationale: Incorrect: flood is not among the extended coverage perils; it is insured through the NFIP.

choices.text: Earthquake and earth movement
choices.rationale: Incorrect: earthquake is not an extended coverage peril.

choices.text: Windstorm and hail
choices.rationale: Correct: § 5401(b) lists windstorm, hail, explosion, riot, riot attending a strike, civil commotion, aircraft, vehicles and smoke.

choices.text: Theft and mysterious disappearance
choices.rationale: Incorrect: theft is not listed; broad form adds burglary damage, not theft of property.

questions.explanation: § 5401(b) defines extended coverage as insurance against direct loss by windstorm, hail, explosion, riot, riot attending a strike, civil commotion, aircraft, vehicles and smoke. Broad form coverage (§ 5401(c)) adds perils such as weight of ice and snow, falling objects, freezing and collapse.
questions.memoryTip: Extended coverage = WHARVES: Windstorm, Hail, Aircraft, Riot (and civil commotion), Vehicles, Explosion, Smoke.

questions.scenario: Luis insures his four-unit rental building through the FAIR Plan. He worries that if a fire makes the apartments untenantable, he will lose his rental income while repairs are made.
questions.stem: Which Article 54 coverage addresses this concern?

choices.text: Sprinkler leakage insurance
choices.rationale: Incorrect: that covers damage from leaking sprinklers, not lost rent.

choices.text: Rent insurance (an additional perils coverage)
choices.rationale: Correct: § 5401(d)(3) defines rent insurance as coverage against actual loss of rental income when property is rendered untenantable by an insured peril.

choices.text: Vandalism and malicious mischief insurance
choices.rationale: Incorrect: VMM covers damage caused by vandals, not loss of income.

choices.text: Extended coverage
choices.rationale: Incorrect: extended coverage adds perils such as windstorm and hail; it does not cover lost income.

questions.explanation: Article 54 lets the association write 'additional perils coverage' with its fire, extended coverage and broad form policies: vandalism and malicious mischief, sprinkler leakage, rent insurance, and business interruption insurance (§ 5401(d)). Rent insurance replaces actual lost rental income while the property is untenantable from an insured peril.
questions.memoryTip: Lost rent? Rent insurance.

questions.stem: Under Article 54, when may the NY Property Insurance Underwriting Association offer homeowners insurance?

choices.text: Whenever any applicant requests a homeowners policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect: homeowners insurance through the association is tied to a superintendent's determination of necessity.

choices.text: Only for homes within one mile of the shore
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the one-mile figure is the minimum C-MAP eligibility area, not the homeowners trigger.

choices.text: After the superintendent determines it is necessary
choices.rationale: Correct: §§ 5402(f) and 5412(b) tie homeowners coverage to a determination of necessity made after a hearing.

choices.text: Never, because it writes only commercial risks
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the association insures residential property, and homeowners insurance is authorized upon a determination of necessity.

questions.explanation: § 5402(f): the association shall offer homeowners insurance upon a determination of necessity by the superintendent under § 5412. § 5412(b) requires a hearing and a finding that meaningful coverage is unavailable in the voluntary market; when availability is restored, the association suspends underwriting for that market.
questions.memoryTip: FAIR Plan homeowners = only when the superintendent says the market needs it.

questions.scenario: Grace owns a single-family home on Long Island, half a mile from the bay. Three insurers have declined her homeowners application, and she asks her agent what to do next.
questions.stem: What is the best next step for the agent?

choices.text: Submit her through C-MAP to reach participating private insurers
choices.rationale: Correct: C-MAP is a voluntary mechanism to give coastal personal residential risks access to participating private market insurers.

choices.text: Apply to the NFIP for a homeowners policy with flood included
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the NFIP sells flood insurance only; it does not issue homeowners policies.

choices.text: Tell her C-MAP will issue her a state-backed homeowners policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect: C-MAP itself does not issue policies; participating private insurers do.

choices.text: Advise her that coastal homes cannot be insured in New York
choices.rationale: Incorrect: NY created C-MAP precisely to improve access to coverage for coastal homes.

questions.explanation: Ins. Law § 5414 requires the association to run the Coastal Market Assistance Program, a voluntary mechanism through which insurers, agents and brokers facilitate access to participating private market insurers for personal residential property risks in coastal areas. Properties within one mile of the shore are eligible at a minimum.
questions.memoryTip: C-MAP = the map back to the private market for coastal homes.

keyPoints.label: C-MAP is for coastal personal residential risks

questions.stem: Which property falls within the minimum C-MAP eligibility that NY Insurance Law § 5414 guarantees?

choices.text: A home half a mile from an inland reservoir
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a reservoir is not among the waters the statute defines as 'shore.'

choices.text: A warehouse a quarter mile from the ocean
choices.rationale: Incorrect: C-MAP is for personal residential property risks, not commercial warehouses.

choices.text: A home three miles from Long Island Sound
choices.rationale: Incorrect: three miles is beyond the one-mile statutory minimum (the association may, but need not, go further).

choices.text: A home half a mile from Lake Ontario
choices.rationale: Correct: the statute's 'shore' includes Lake Ontario, and properties within one mile of the shore must be eligible.

questions.explanation: § 5414(c): at a minimum, properties within one mile of the shore are eligible. 'Shore' means salt-water ocean, sound, bay, inlet, Lake Erie, Lake Ontario, the Saint Lawrence River, the Hudson River or the Niagara River, measured from mean high water. The association may adopt more expansive standards, and C-MAP serves personal residential risks.
questions.memoryTip: C-MAP shore = salt water plus the Great Lakes and big rivers named in the law, within a mile.

keyPoints.label: Within one mile of the shore

questions.stem: Who administers New York's Coastal Market Assistance Program (C-MAP)?

choices.text: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
choices.rationale: Incorrect: FEMA manages the NFIP, a federal flood program.

choices.text: The NY Property Insurance Underwriting Association
choices.rationale: Correct: § 5414(c) states the association shall administer C-MAP.

choices.text: The Excess Line Association of New York (ELANY)
choices.rationale: Incorrect: ELANY records and stamps excess line placements.

choices.text: The New York Automobile Insurance Plan
choices.rationale: Incorrect: that plan is the residual market for auto insurance.

questions.explanation: Under § 5414, the NY Property Insurance Underwriting Association (the FAIR Plan) creates and administers C-MAP, advised by a C-MAP agents advisory council made up of producers who sell homeowners insurance in the areas C-MAP serves.
questions.memoryTip: The FAIR Plan runs the C-MAP.

questions.stem: A New York resident seeking an excess line broker's license must already hold which NY license?

choices.text: Insurance agent license
choices.rationale: Incorrect: § 2105 requires a broker license, not an agent license.

choices.text: Public adjuster license
choices.rationale: Incorrect: adjusters handle claims; the law ties the excess line license to the broker license.

choices.text: Insurance broker license
choices.rationale: Correct: § 2105(a) lets the superintendent issue an excess line license to a person licensed as an insurance broker under § 2104.

choices.text: Insurance consultant license
choices.rationale: Incorrect: consultants give advice for a fee; they are not the qualifying license.

questions.explanation: § 2105(a): the superintendent may issue an excess line broker's license to a person or entity licensed as an insurance broker under § 2104 (or licensed as an excess line broker in its home state, subject to reciprocity). The excess line license expires with the qualifying broker license (§ 2105(d)).
questions.memoryTip: Excess line = Broker plus.

questions.scenario: An excess line broker is placing coverage for a New York client whose risk is not on the export list. Two authorized insurers that the broker reasonably believed might write the risk have declined it. The broker has not contacted any other authorized insurer.
questions.stem: What must the broker do before placing the risk with an unauthorized insurer?

choices.text: Obtain a declination from a third qualifying authorized insurer
choices.rationale: Correct: diligent effort generally means declinations from three authorized insurers that might consider writing the risk.

choices.text: Nothing more; two declinations satisfy diligent effort
choices.rationale: Incorrect: two declinations are allowed only for the specific professional liability risks listed in Reg 41; the general rule is three.

choices.text: Have the client sign a waiver of the diligent effort rule
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a personal client cannot waive the requirement; the written-request exception is for exempt commercial purchasers.

choices.text: Get approval from the superintendent for each placement
choices.rationale: Incorrect: no case-by-case approval is required; the broker documents declinations on the affidavit.

questions.explanation: Ins. Law § 2118(b)(4) and Reg 41 § 27.3(a): unless an exception applies, the risk must be declined by at least three authorized insurers, each authorized to write the kind of insurance and which the broker had reason to believe might consider writing it. The declinations are recorded on the affidavit.
questions.memoryTip: Three strikes in the licensed market, then you may go excess.

keyPoints.label: From authorized insurers that might write it

questions.scenario: A broker's three declinations all came from authorized insurers in the same insurance group. The companies share underwriting and do not compete with each other for this type of coverage.
questions.stem: How are these declinations treated for diligent effort purposes?

choices.text: They count as three, since each insurer is separately licensed
choices.rationale: Incorrect: separate licenses are not enough when the affiliates do not operate as distinct, competing entities.

choices.text: They do not satisfy the requirement, since the affiliates don't compete
choices.rationale: Correct: declinations from affiliates count only if they operate as distinct and autonomous entities that compete for the coverage.

choices.text: They count as three if the broker notes the group on the affidavit
choices.rationale: Incorrect: disclosure on the affidavit does not cure the affiliate problem.

choices.text: They count only if the unauthorized insurer is in the same group
choices.rationale: Incorrect: affiliation with the unauthorized insurer makes the problem worse, not better.

questions.explanation: Ins. Law § 2118(b)(3)(D) and Reg 41 § 27.3(c): declinations from authorized insurers that are affiliates of, or under common control with, each other or the unauthorized insurer don't meet the requirement unless they operate as distinct and autonomous entities and compete with each other for the same type of coverage.
questions.memoryTip: One family saying no three times is still one 'no.'

keyPoints.label: Must be distinct and competing to count

questions.scenario: A client's estate needs $5,000,000 of property coverage. After a diligent search, an authorized insurer offers to write $2,000,000 but no authorized insurer will write more.
questions.stem: How much coverage may the excess line broker place with an unauthorized insurer?

choices.rationale: Incorrect: the amount procurable from authorized insurers must be placed there; only the excess may go to an unauthorized insurer.
Incorrect: $2,000,000 is the authorized insurer's share.
Incorrect: this adds the amounts instead of subtracting, and exceeds the coverage needed.
Correct: $5,000,000 needed − $2,000,000 procurable from authorized insurers = $3,000,000 excess.

questions.explanation: Reg 41 § 27.3(d) and § 2118(b)(3)(A): if less than the full amount can be obtained from authorized insurers, the excess line broker may procure from an unauthorized insurer only the excess over the amount obtainable from authorized insurers: $5,000,000 − $2,000,000 = $3,000,000.
questions.memoryTip: Authorized first; unauthorized only for what's left.

keyPoints.label: Authorized market amount must be used
Only the excess may be placed

questions.stem: For each declining authorized insurer, the excess line affidavit must record all of these items EXCEPT:

choices.text: The name of the authorized insurer
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: the insurer's name is required.

choices.text: The date of the declination
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: the declination date is required.

choices.text: The reason the insurer declined
choices.rationale: Correct: § 2118(b)(3)(C) says the broker is not required to record the reason for the declination.

choices.text: The insurer's NAIC code
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: the NAIC code is required.

questions.explanation: § 2118(b)(3)(C): the licensee or affirming broker records the name, date of declination and NAIC code of each declining authorized insurer and the information that formed the basis for believing it might write the coverage. The representative's name, affiliation and the reason for the declination need not be recorded.
questions.memoryTip: Who, when, which code — not why.

questions.scenario: Elena's waterfront home is worth far more than the maximum building limit available from the NFIP. She already has an NFIP policy and wants additional flood coverage above it.
questions.stem: How does Reg 41 treat placing this excess flood coverage with an unauthorized insurer?

choices.text: It is on the export list, so declinations are not required
choices.rationale: Correct: Reg 41 § 27.3(g) lists flood insurance in excess of the federal program's maximum limits among coverages exempt from the declination requirement.

choices.text: Three NFIP declinations are required before placement
choices.rationale: Incorrect: this coverage is on the export list, so declinations are not required.

choices.text: It is prohibited because flood is a federal program
choices.rationale: Incorrect: Reg 41 expressly contemplates excess flood coverage in the excess line market.

choices.text: The FAIR Plan must first decline the flood coverage
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the FAIR Plan writes fire and related perils, not flood.

questions.explanation: Under Ins. Law § 2118(b)(4), the superintendent may exempt coverages from the declination requirement. Reg 41 § 27.3(g) lists them — the 'export list' — including 'Flood Insurance Excess of Maximum Limits available from the Federal Flood Program' and primary flood coverage on property not eligible for the federal program.
questions.memoryTip: Above the NFIP cap? Straight to the export list.

keyPoints.label: Coverage is on the export list

questions.stem: Under Reg 41, what is the status of an excess line policy before the insured receives the required written notice about the unauthorized insurer?

choices.text: Fully binding, with the notice due at renewal
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the notice is a precondition to the policy binding the insured, not a renewal formality.

choices.text: Not binding on the insured, and no premium is due
choices.rationale: Correct: § 27.15(e) says no excess line policy is binding on the insured, and no premium is due, until the notice is given.

choices.text: Void, and the broker must refund all commissions
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the regulation does not void the policy or address commissions this way.

choices.text: Converted to coverage backed by the security funds
choices.rationale: Incorrect: unauthorized insurers are never backed by the NY security funds.

questions.explanation: 11 NYCRR 27.15(e): the policy is not binding on the insured, and no premium is due and payable, until the insured gets written notice that (1) the insurer is not licensed by or subject to supervision by NY, (2) losses will not be covered by the NY State security funds if it becomes insolvent, and (3) the policy may not be subject to all DFS policy-form regulations.
questions.memoryTip: No warning label, no binding, no bill.

questions.stem: The bold legend required on a written confirmation of an excess line placement warns the insured that:

choices.text: The policy is void if the insurer leaves New York
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the legend says nothing about the insurer leaving the state.

choices.text: A guaranty fund surcharge will be added to the premium
choices.rationale: Incorrect: there is no security fund protection, so there is no such surcharge.

choices.text: NY security funds won't protect against insurer insolvency
choices.rationale: Correct: the legend states the insurer is not licensed or supervised by NY and is not protected by the NY State security funds if insolvent.

choices.text: The excess line broker guarantees payment of all claims
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the broker does not guarantee the insurer's obligations.

questions.explanation: Reg 41 § 27.15(b) requires confirmations of excess line placements to bear, conspicuously in bold type, a legend that the insurer is not licensed by New York, not subject to its supervision, and in the event of insolvency not protected by the New York State security funds, and that the policy may not be subject to all DFS policy-form regulations.
questions.memoryTip: Excess lines = no NY safety net.

questions.scenario: After three authorized insurers decline a client's dwelling fire risk, an excess line broker plans to place it with an unauthorized insurer. The same basic fire coverage is available to the client from the FAIR Plan.
questions.stem: Under Reg 41, what else must happen before the excess line placement?

choices.text: Nothing; FAIR Plan availability is irrelevant to excess lines
choices.rationale: Incorrect: for coverage available from a residual market facility, Reg 41 requires a declination or informed written consent.

choices.text: The superintendent must approve the specific placement
choices.rationale: Incorrect: no individual approval by the superintendent is required.

choices.text: The client must first buy a FAIR Plan policy for one year
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the client is not required to buy the FAIR Plan policy first.

choices.text: A FAIR Plan declination, or written consent after being told of it
choices.rationale: Correct: § 27.3(e)(2) requires a residual market declination unless the insured was advised of its availability and consented in writing.

questions.explanation: Reg 41 § 27.3(e)(2) (and Ins. Law § 2118(e)(2)(B)): for kinds of insurance other than non-commercial auto liability, certain malpractice, and insurance required by law to be written by authorized insurers, a declination from the appropriate residual market facility (such as the FAIR Plan, an Article 54 association) is required unless, before placement, the insured was advised that coverage is available there and consented in writing to the unauthorized insurer.
questions.memoryTip: FAIR Plan available? Get its 'no' — or the client's informed 'yes, go excess' in writing.

keyPoints.label: FAIR Plan is a residual market facility

questions.scenario: An excess line broker delivers a declarations page to a New York client without first having it stamped by the Excess Line Association of New York. Later the client has a covered loss.
questions.stem: What is the effect of the broker's failure to have the document stamped?

choices.text: It is unlawful for the broker, but the coverage stays valid
choices.rationale: Correct: § 2118(b)(6) makes delivering an unstamped document unlawful but says the failure does not affect the validity of the coverage.

choices.text: The policy is void, so the insurer may deny the claim
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the statute expressly preserves the validity of the coverage.

choices.text: Coverage is suspended until the stamp is obtained
choices.rationale: Incorrect: nothing in the law suspends coverage for lack of a stamp.

choices.text: The client must pay a penalty before the claim is paid
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the stamping duty falls on the broker, not the insured.

questions.explanation: Under § 2118(b), the excess line licensee submits declarations pages or cover notes (with the affidavit) to the Excess Line Association of New York for recording and stamping. § 2118(b)(6) makes it unlawful to deliver an unstamped declarations page or cover note in NY, but 'a licensee's failure to comply … shall not affect the validity of the coverage.'
questions.memoryTip: No stamp: the broker is in trouble, the client is still covered.

questions.stem: Before placing business with an unauthorized insurer, a NY excess line broker must verify that the insurer is:

choices.text: Licensed in New York for the line of insurance
choices.rationale: Incorrect: if it were licensed in NY it would be an authorized insurer, not an excess line insurer.

choices.text: A member of the NY property insurance association
choices.rationale: Incorrect: FAIR Plan membership applies to authorized insurers writing fire coverage in NY.

choices.text: Authorized in its home jurisdiction to write the policy
choices.rationale: Correct: § 2118(b) requires the broker to ascertain and verify that the insurer is authorized in its domiciliary jurisdiction to write the proposed policy.

choices.text: Covered by the New York State security funds
choices.rationale: Incorrect: unauthorized insurers are not protected by the NY security funds.

questions.explanation: § 2118(a)(1) requires due care in selecting the unauthorized insurer, and § 2118(b) requires the licensee to ascertain and verify that the insurer is authorized in its domiciliary jurisdiction to write the policy. An insurer is not unacceptable solely because it has held that home authority for less than three years.
questions.memoryTip: Unauthorized HERE, but must be authorized at HOME.

questions.stem: In an excess line placement, the total cost form is intended to:

choices.text: Prove that three authorized insurers declined the risk
choices.rationale: Incorrect: that is the purpose of the affidavit.

choices.text: Show the insured the full cost, including non-premium charges
choices.rationale: Correct: the form discloses the all-in cost of the placement to the insured.

choices.text: List coverages that are exempt from declinations
choices.rationale: Incorrect: that is the export list in Reg 41.

choices.text: Transfer the policy to an authorized insurer at renewal
choices.rationale: Incorrect: no such transfer function exists.

questions.explanation: Excess line placements can carry charges in addition to premium. The total cost form presents the insured with the complete cost of the coverage so the insured can make an informed decision. (Confirm the current required contents against DFS/ELANY requirements.)
questions.memoryTip: Total cost form = the out-the-door price.

verification.notes: Required contents of the total cost form not located in the Reg 41 sections retrieved; verify before publishing.

questions.stem: In New York, an excess line policy is issued by an insurer that is:

choices.text: Licensed in New York as a domestic insurer
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a NY-licensed insurer is an authorized (admitted) insurer.

choices.text: A residual market facility created by statute
choices.rationale: Incorrect: residual market facilities (like the FAIR Plan) are separate from the excess line market.

choices.text: A federal agency such as FEMA
choices.rationale: Incorrect: FEMA administers the NFIP; it is not an excess line insurer.

choices.text: Not authorized to transact business in New York
choices.rationale: Correct: excess line coverage is procured from insurers not authorized in NY (the nonadmitted market).

questions.explanation: Ins. Law § 2105 authorizes excess line brokers to procure policies from insurers that are not authorized to transact business in New York. Reg 41 defines an unauthorized insurer as any insurer that is not an authorized insurer (including certain syndicates and exchanges such as Lloyd's).
questions.memoryTip: Excess lines = the nonadmitted market.
